english.title: Sabotage
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) engaged in conduct that resulted in damage to an asset, namely **(..SPECIFY ASSET..), intending such conduct to result in damage to that asset, or being reckless as to whether it would result in damage to it, when you knew or ought to have known that such conduct was for a purpose that was prejudicial to the safety or interests of the United Kingdom, and the conduct was carried out for or on behalf of a foreign power when you knew, or having regard to other known matters, ought to have known, that to be the case
english.legislation: Contrary to section 12 of the National Security Act 2023.
english.pointstoprove:

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure

english.notes:
(i) This offence no longer applies from 7th July 2026 due to changes made by the National Security (State Threats) Act 2026. For the offence applying after this date, see H102842.
(ii) Prosecution of this offence requires the consent of the Attorney General, section 37 of the National Security Act 2023.
(iii) This offence applies whether the person’s conduct takes place in the United Kingdom or elsewhere and whether the asset is in the United Kingdom or elsewhere. Extra-territorial jurisdiction is necessary because there are important assets overseas, damage to which could be prejudicial to the safety or interests of the UK, section 12(2).
(iv) The person's conduct must meet the "foreign power condition" as set out in section 31.
(v) Additional powers of entry, search and seizure are provided in Schedule 2 where there are reasonable grounds for suspecting that this offence has been, or is about to be, committed.
